In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His words: ﴿You see no imbalance in the creation of the Most Gracious﴾, meaning rather it is harmonious and uniform, with no difference, no discord, no opposition, no deficiency, no defect and no flaw. For this reason He said: ﴿Then look again; do you see any rifts?﴾, meaning: look at the sky and consider it carefully; do you see in it any defect, deficiency, flaw or cracks?

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Thawri and others said concerning His words ﴿Do you see any rifts?﴾: meaning cracks.

﴿while it is weary﴾. Ibn Abbas said: meaning exhausted. Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: al-Hasir is the one who is worn out from fatigue.

The meaning of the verse: even if you repeat your gaze, however much you repeat it, your sight will return to you, ﴿dazed﴾ from seeing any defect or flaw, ﴿while it is weary﴾, meaning exhausted and spent from fatigue due to repeated looking, and seeing no deficiency.

Allah the Exalted says: "And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Jahannam (Hell), and wretched is the destination." That is, wretched is the final abode and the place of return.

"When they are cast into it, they will hear from it a roaring (shahiq)." Ibn Jarir said: this means shouting.

"While it boils up." Al-Thawri said: it seethes with them as a small amount of grain seethes in a large quantity of water.

* *

His saying: "It almost bursts apart from fury" means that it nearly splits apart, some of it from the rest, because of its intense anger at them and its rage against them. "Every time a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them, 'Did no warner come to you?' They will say, 'Yes, indeed, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said: Allah has revealed nothing; you are only in great error.'"

Here Allah mentions His justice toward His creation, and that He does not punish anyone except after the proof has been established against him and a messenger has been sent to him, as He said: "And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger" [al-Isra' 15]. And Allah the Exalted said: "Until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, 'Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?' They will say, 'Yes, but the word of punishment has been fulfilled against the disbelievers'" [al-Zumar 71].

Thus they turned blame upon themselves and regretted when regret would not benefit them, and they said: "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze." That is: if we had possessed minds by which we benefited, or had listened to what Allah sent down of the truth, we would not have been in the state of disbelief in Allah and deception by Him in which we were. But we had no understanding by which we comprehended what the messengers brought, nor did we have a mind that guided us to follow them.
